SOCIAL NETWORKING BEFORE SOCIAL MEDIA: FOOTBALL STICKERS!

🎙️ Massimo Caputi · Federico De Nigro (Universal Music) · Martina Limoni (Panini) · Daniele Calonaci (Stellantis/Jeep) · Jacopo Pulcini (Genoa)

👉 This was the deepest session of the morning, almost an elegy to physical objects and to the slow, deep engagement that grows around them, and I enjoyed every minute. Martina Limoni from Panini explained why swapping stickers still matters: a child who wants a card has to talk to another child, offer something and sometimes accept a no. That is social networking with real stakes, and Panini has been running it since 1961.

Massimo Caputi said that when he started commentating foreign leagues on Telemontecarlo in the mid-80s, Panini albums were his database, because nowhere else had the players’ faces and basic stats. Jacopo Pulcini added that Genoa is seeing its season-ticket base get younger, even though the city is one of the oldest in Italy.

The common thread was passion handed down: a father restoring an old Jeep with his son, parents getting back into the album through their kids, and a club you never change. Federico De Nigro described how Universal gives its vinyl rarity levels, borrowed from video games, so collectors have something to hunt for. I’ve been digging for records for most of my life, so I didn’t need convincing, and it was good to hear a room full of marketers agree that the hunt is the point.

📍 Live from #SFS26 at the Allianz Stadium, Torino

Engagement Stage, 11.30–12.15

90 MINUTES ARE NO LONGER ENOUGH

🎙️ Monica Bertini (Mediaset) · Michele Ciccarese (Lega Serie A, Commercial & Marketing) · Luisella Fusco (Lega Serie A) · Nino Ragosta (Fantacalcio) · Emiliano Garofalo (Haier) · Francesco Furlan (Volkswagen) 

👉 Serie A is innovating for real, and I’ll say it even with all the structural limits this market carries. Luisella Fusco gave the best example of both: to run the referee camera live, Lega Serie A had to set up its own private 5G bubble at each stadium, because Italian stadium connectivity is behind Germany’s. It also put an editorial supervisor on that single feed, and it was the first of the big five leagues to put a referee camera on air live. Now the league wants the referee audio back, which depends on talks with the federation.

Michele Ciccarese explained the plan behind the title. The league has built the tools to talk to fans from Monday to Saturday: the Lissone broadcast centre, which feeds 56 broadcasters in more than 180 countries, its own in-house radio, and now Fantacalcio. Nino Ragosta’s numbers explain why: 8 million people in the database and 3 million playing every week, in leagues that live in WhatsApp groups. Fantacalcio fans also give the league a slice of their relationships, which no other channel gets.

The strategic move is a collective CRM, built by the league for all 20 clubs on top of the Fantacalcio base, with Atalanta, Roma and Juventus already testing ways to reach their own fans inside the app. The next step involves broadcasters: DAZN subscribers taking part in votes and awards during the live match. I’ve spent years arguing that nobody owns a fan, and this is the most serious attempt I’ve seen in Italy to connect the league, the clubs and the broadcasters around the fan.

📍 Live from #SFS26 at the Allianz Stadium, Torino Industry Stage, 11.00–11.35

THE AI GAME 🎙️ Ivan Ortenzi (SFS) · Roberto Morucci (AWS) · Luisella Fusco (Lega Serie A) · Lorenzo Antognoli (Inter Football Innovation Hub) · Luigi Capitanio (Deloitte)

👉 It was refreshing to hear an AI panel full of things already in production, and Ivan Ortenzi kept it there by pushing for practical cases instead of strategy talk.

Luisella Fusco gave the clearest picture of what a league can do. Lega Serie A has a natural-language stats tool that TV commentators already use and broadcasters will get next. It is building its own system to detect and take down illegal streams, separate from Piracy Shield. Every event data point is now certified on blockchain under a “True Data” campaign, because AI makes it possible to scrape match data from video and resell it. The best detail was the Inter title video, made entirely with AI by one person working from Naples, then translated and sent to international broadcasters as part of the rights sales push.

Lorenzo Antognoli explained Inter’s Football Innovation Hub, which produces a report on about 1,000 tactical indicators within three minutes of the final whistle. Inter applies the same approach from the first team down to the youth and women’s teams. Its rule is a good one for any club: buy the technology, keep control of the data, and build in-house the models that carry its football knowledge.

AWS and Deloitte covered the platform and governance side, which every club needs, and the league and the club gave the room the examples.

📍 Live from #SFS26 at the Allianz Stadium, Torino Engagement Stage, 10.05–10.50

WELCOME TO THE ATTENTION ECONOMY! 🎙️ Sergio Amati (IAB) · Riccardo Russo (Chiamarsi Bomber) · Andrea David Rizzi (YouTube Italy & Portugal) · Alessandra Sangalli (TikTok) · Stefano Russo (YouGov Italia) · Federico Felletti (creator)

👉 The panel opened on the obvious, with a show of hands on who can watch 90 minutes without touching their phone, and got better as it went on. YouGov put a number on the obvious: Italians who follow Serie A spend about 8 hours 20 minutes a week on football, which comes to roughly 200 million hours. The live match is still the backbone at around 200 minutes, and everything else flows around it.

The two best contributions came from TikTok and the creator. Alessandra Sangalli described Atletico Madrid running a multicultural social team and using geo-targeted distribution, so each country sees a different version of the content. Federico Felletti told the story of an Inter and Nike kit ad that performed on his channel like organic content. Then he asked the question clubs should answer: if fans live on these platforms, why don't the budgets follow them?

Andrea Rizzi from YouTube said 45 billion hours of sport were watched on the platform last year, and his advice to clubs was to become obsessed with their data. That's exactly why I built the YouTube Football Tracker, which follows 101 club and league channels every day. This morning in Torino it felt like the room was asking for it.

Three things in the recording are hard to make out, so check them before posting: the 200 million hours figure, YouTube's 45 billion hours, and that the creator's question was about budgets following the audience. I left out the CazéTV and IShowSpeed examples because the transcript garbles them. Tell me if you want either one back in.
Will start live blogging SFS 2026 in Torino at Allianz Stadium today

🏟️ The SFS - Social Football Summit is at the Allianz Stadium in Torino (my city) this week, which means that for once I get to an industry event without an airport, a hotel or a taxi queue, and I sleep at home between the two days.

🗓️ The programme has more than a hundred sessions across three main stages and a long list of side rooms, and since I now have Claude Code open on my laptop pretty much all day, I pulled the whole schedule into a small interactive page built for an audience of exactly one. The three stages sit side by side with time running down the page, it suggests what I should follow based on the work I do, and as soon as I star a session everything that overlaps it fades out, so the clashes are obvious and the decision stays with me. It took less time than reading the official schedule twice.

💡 It made me think about the word personalisation. For years it described a platform watching our clicks and guessing what we wanted. What I am doing now is closer to "give me the data and I will build my own view", for one event, one day, one person, and then throw it away or keep it.

🛠️ In the last few months, with a similar but often more sophisticated setup, I have built three websites and ten dataviz pages and multiple apps, and this planner is the smallest and probably the most useful of them all.

❓ So here is my question for anyone building event platforms and fan products: are we heading into a time when the organiser publishes clean data and each of us builds the view we need? I can't speak for everyone else, but I am already doing it.

 💻 If you are at SFS today, come and find me. I'll be the one with the scarf and the laptop open.
